Diogenes Laertius

Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VII (On the Stoics)

The most important continuous ancient source for Stoic logic — 40 paragraphs covering lekta, axiomata, the five indemonstrables, and the conditional. Referenced throughout PHIL 705 as D.L. VII.

Bobzien, S., 2019

Stoic Sequent Logic and Proof Theory

Shows that Stoic analysis is structurally closest to backward proof search in substructural sequent logics — closer to logic programming than to Gentzen's natural deduction. Transforms the Session 12 picture of what the themata actually do.

proof theory · sequent logic · themata · indemonstrables · analysis · substructural

Open PhilPapers →
paperOpen Accessadvanced

Bobzien, S. & Dyckhoff, R., 2018

Analyticity, Balance and Non-admissibility of Cut in Stoic Logic

Proves decidability of Stoic propositional logic and shows Cut is not admissible in the standard Stoic system. Technical companion to the sequent logic paper above.

proof theory · cut rule · decidability · stoic logic · sequent

Open PhilPapers (open access) →
paperLibrary Accessadvanced

Bobzien, S., 1999

Chrysippus' Theory of Causes

Systematic reconstruction of Chrysippus's causal theory grounded in the Stoic tenets that causes are bodies, that they are relative, and that all causation traces to the active pneuma. Challenges the standard taxonomy and argues antecedent and principal causes are alternatives, not cooperating factors — directly relevant to the cylinder argument in Session 16.

causation · chrysippus · fate · pneuma · determinism · cylinder argument · principal cause

Find in Library →

Published in Ierodiakonou (ed.), Topics in Stoic Philosophy, OUP 1999. Available via university libraries. Core arguments also covered in Bobzien, Determinism and Freedom in Stoic Philosophy (OUP 1998), Ch. 1 — which is more widely available.

bookLibrary Accessadvanced

Bobzien, S., 1998

Determinism and Freedom in Stoic Philosophy

The definitive monograph on Stoic determinism, fate, and compatibilism. Chapters 1–2 cover Chrysippus's theory of causes and the cylinder argument in depth. The most important secondary source for Block G.

determinism · fate · compatibilism · causation · cylinder argument · chrysippus · free will

Between Dialectic and Formalism: A Comparative Study of Stoic and Contemporary Logics

Bobzien, S., 2020

Frege Plagiarized the Stoics

Argues that Frege absorbed Stoic logic from Prantl's 1855 History of Western Logic without attribution — documenting 120+ parallels, including cases where Frege's errors track Prantl's misrepresentations. Central paper for Session 19.

frege · chrysippus · lekton · sinn · plagiarism · history of logic · prantl
